title: Aligned special dataset input contract audit
scope: Read-only structural inspection of attachment 3 and 4 aligned files. No labels, video inspection, inference, training, hyperparameter choice, threshold choice or performance estimates.
index_convention: All sequence indices are zero-based. All reported ranges are half-open [start,end).

canonical_input_contract.sequence_mask: bool [B,50] from provided text_bert attention channel, retained independently of modality values
canonical_input_contract.content_mask: sequence_mask excluding CLS and SEP, with special IDs verified
canonical_input_contract.modality_zero_mask: Within content_mask only; whole-feature-vector exact zeros recorded separately from padding and never deleted or compacted
canonical_input_contract.text_route: Attachment 3 has no precomputed 768-dimensional text. A deployment-consistent text_bert encoding route must also be used during train/validation, or equivalence to stored text must be explicitly established before mixed routes. Selecting architecture/thresholds on special files is prohibited.
canonical_input_contract.text_missing_semantics: No internal text token/attention gaps observed in attachment 3. This does not establish a general text-missing encoding. Retain pre-corruption sequence_mask separately when simulating text missingness.

limitations: All-zero content vectors are an observable numeric property. These files provide no explicit corruption/provenance mask proving each zero was introduced by a specific synthetic missingness mechanism.
CLS/SEP audio and vision rows are zero by observed convention and are not counted as missing content.
Precomputed text padding embeddings in attachment 4 can be nonzero. Neither text embedding values nor a corrupted text feature mask determines sequence padding.
Attachment 4 13.pkl has vision all zero at positions [0,50), including all 30 content positions [1,31). This is preserved and flagged without modifying source data.
No timestamps or per-feature physical meanings are inferred from shared sequence shape.
